messages:
mina (pm): thinking out loud — can we add a lightweight periodic 'version-synchrony' ping from the SDKs so the console can show per-tenant version freshness?
rajarshi (eng): curious — is this a push from the client or a passive inference from requests?
sarah (platform): +1 on an explicit ping. passive hooks are noisy and brittle for long idle tenants. ping could be an opt-in admin flag.
luis (eng-sre): concern: any extra pings count toward quota unless we special-case them. we should avoid billing customers for health telemetry.
mina (pm): agree. plan: 1) ping over control plane (not generation endpoint) 2) mark it as non-billable in metering 3) sample if needed for scale.
rajarshi (eng): technical detail: control-plane API would need to accept header `x-rw-version-heartbeat: <semver>` and a tenant id. small payload. we can authenticate via existing API key.
sarah (platform): UX side — console would show a freshness column (green/yellow/red) based on last heartbeat. also a hover to explain the ping and opt-out. avoid alarming language.
luis (eng-sre): from infra POV: implement a lightweight ingestion path that writes to a hot-timeseries store, TTL 90 days. expose a single query for dashboards. avoid touching token-metering pipeline.
mina (pm): telemetry events: `version_heartbeat.received` (tags: tenant, version, sdk), `version_heartbeat.missed_alert` (for 7d no heartbeat). keep event size minimal.
rajarshi (eng): rollout strategy: start with SDKs (node, python) as opt-in feature flag for next minor release. enable platform-side parsing for unknown version strings.
sarah (platform): console: add a grouped row to Routes/Usage table + a filter to surface tenants with >=30d drift. also show a one-click 'message tenant' action linking to workspace.
luis (eng-sre): sampling: start with 100% for paid tenants, 1% for free trial to reduce churn. can increase if storage cheap.
mina (pm): do we need privacy/legal signoff? heartbeat only carries semver and sdk name. no PII. I'll run it by legal but low risk.
rajarshi (eng): code snippet for the client (proposal):
```
fetch('https://control.redwood.ai/v1/heartbeat', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer <key>', 'x-rw-version-heartbeat': 'sdk-js/2.1.0' },
  body: '{}'
})
```
sarah (platform): nice. console copy should say "Version heartbeat is non-billable telemetry that helps you stay on supported SDKs."
luis (eng-sre): ops note: ensure heartbeats are idempotent and rate-limited server-side (e.g., 1/min per token) to avoid thundering herd from clients on reconnect.
mina (pm): monitoring/alerts: create a synthetic that checks % of tenants with heartbeat in last 7 days — if it drops >30% during rollout we pause.
rajarshi (eng): telemetry naming & metrics: `heartbeat.ingest_rate`, `heartbeat.unique_tenants_7d`, `heartbeat.version_diversity`. export to console and prometheus.
sarah (platform): console UX: if tenant shows red >30d drift, surface a non-dismissible banner with docs link only for account admins; don't automatically show to end-users.
luis (eng-sre): edge case: customers behind strict firewalls could block calls to control plane. sample fallback: derive version from the first generation request header as before. mark it as inferred.
mina (pm): good. timeline: proposal -> prototype this sprint -> SDK opt-in next minor -> platform rollout + console flags in 3 weeks.
rajarshi (eng): I'll open an internal RFC and prototype the endpoint. tagging: @sarah for console mocks, @luis for infra constraints.
sarah (platform): I'll sketch mockups tomorrow and drop in #design.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: control-plane-heartbeat-api -> staging at 2025-05-02T14:00Z
mina (pm): thanks — can someone add a short blurb to release notes about heartbeat being opt-in and non-billable?
luis (eng-sre): I'll add the billing exemption and TTL details to the infra PR. :+1:
rajarshi (eng): ok, moving to RFC. posting link when ready.
mina (pm): great, closing the loop. :tada:
